messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Global routing anomaly detected for /v1/generate — p95 latency jump + increased 5xx rate. Affected regions: eu-west (client-visible), us-west (backend surge). Alert id: GLOB-1928604321. See runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/routing-steering
Dmitri (oncall): Oncall here, ack. I’m seeing p95 in eu-west ~1.4s and error rate ~3.7% for generate. Starting quick checks — health, route table, recent config changes.
Dmitri (oncall): Running quick probe to origin from eu-edge:
```bash
curl -sS -w '%{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null 'https://eu-edge.redwood/api/route-check?path=/v1/generate'
# result: 0.32s (but some probes routed to us-west backend)
```
Carmen (networking): saw an automated rollout last night to latency-steering v2. It introduced a weighting delta when peers report staleness. Could be related. Checking LB steering logs.
Ben (eng-platform): I’m pulling the steering metrics and recent policy commits. No infra deploys in last 24h except the steering config push at 03:12 UTC.
Eli (support): Customer ticket from ACME saying big slowdowns around 03:40 UTC, matches alert. They report timeouts ~500ms to 3s.
Dmitri (oncall): Quick hypothesis: some eu DNS caches still had old TTLs while steering changed weights -> a fraction of EU traffic got sent to us-west with higher RTT and occasional backend throttles, causing tail latency and retries -> more load in us-west -> cascading.
Alice (SRE): Can we confirm DNS TTLs? Show dig from multiple clients.
Dmitri (oncall): From three vantage points:
```bash
# eu-test1
dig +short edge.redwood.example @8.8.8.8
# -> 1.2.3.4 (eu)
# eu-test2 (ISP cache)
dig +short edge.redwood.example @8.26.56.26
# -> 5.6.7.8 (us-west)  # stale mapping
```
Carmen (networking): ack, seen mismatched answers. TTL on the record is 300s, but some upstream caches respected much longer. Also noticed steering controller emitted a fallback pin for some client prefixes due to transient probe failures. That fallback logic looks buggy — it pinned by POP id, but later the pin table was not cleared properly.
Ben (eng-platform): Rolling back steering v2 to v1 is low-risk and should restore deterministic region pinning. Suggest toggling steering to static-runbook mode while we repair pin clearing. Thoughts?
Dmitri (oncall): Agree — mitigation: 1) disable latency-steering autoweights -> force pin-by-region; 2) flush edge DNS by incrementing A record version (bump CNAME alias) to force caches to re-resolve; 3) apply temporary weight cap on us-west to avoid overload.
Carmen (networking): I can flip steering to static now and set us-west cap to 20% of normal. Doing step 1 & 3.
Carmen (networking): :white_check_mark: static steering enabled. us-west cap set. Monitoring.
Dmitri (oncall): Doing DNS bump: incrementing cname alias token. Note: this is a soft DNS nudge, some caches still honor old mapping until expiry.
Ben (eng-platform): Kicking rollback for steering v2 -> v1 via controller: `controller rollback steering v2 --to v1 --reason "panic-rollback"`.
Ben (eng-platform): :white_check_mark: rollback accepted by controller. Controllers report steady-state.
Alice (SRE): Observability: error rate in eu-west dropping from 3.7% -> 0.6% over last 120s, p95 down to 0.48s. Good sign.
Eli (support): Notifying ACME that we saw a routing steering anomaly and applied mitigations — ETA for full resolution ~10–20m. Drafting status message.
Dmitri (oncall): Still seeing ~0.2% of requests routing to us-west from EU based on trace sampling — likely from stubborn caches. We'll keep monitoring and escalate to CDN vendor if it persists.
Carmen (networking): Filed ticket with CDN provider: ticket #CDN-7654 — asked for cache purge on edge entries for edge.redwood.example. Also added a fix to pin clearing logic to prevent stale pin entries (will go through review).
Ben (eng-platform): Opening a follow-up task to add a forced TTL reset path to the runbook so we can avoid manual cname bumps next time.
Alice (SRE): Handing off to Carmen for next 2h for remediation & postmortem work. Dmitri, stand by for oncall wrap.
Dmitri (oncall): Handoff accepted. I’ll write the incident summary and update the incident channel.
Eli (support): Customer comms sent: "We're mitigating a routing issue causing elevated latency — routing control changes applied; monitoring indicates recovery. We'll follow up with details."
Carmen (networking): Continuing root-cause: steering controller fallback code pinned by POP id but never cleared under condition X. Patch queued: PR #4123. Postmortem items: clearer TTL guidance, add e2e test for pin clearing, make steering fallback logs more verbose.
Dmitri (oncall): Postmortem owners: Carmen (networking) and Ben (platform). Severity: sev2 (customer impact but mitigations applied quickly).
Alice (SRE): Final check: p95 eu-west now 0.36s, error rate back to baseline 0.1%. Closing pager.
incident-bot: Pager closed by Dmitri (oncall). Duration: ~28m.
Dmitri (oncall): Thanks team. Follow-up: Carmen/Ben coordinate on postmortem, include timeline and customer impact metrics. Will sync with ACME tomorrow for RCA if they request.
Carmen (networking): Adding remediation checklist to runbook and scheduling a review with CDN vendor.
Ben (eng-platform): Adding automated smoke that validates steering->dns consistency across 5 external resolvers.
Eli (support): Marking affected customer tickets as "mitigated" and linking incident thread.
Alice (SRE): Good job. Closing thread once postmortem PR is merged.
Dmitri (oncall): Closing now.
